message.content:
**Decision: bought 44 shares of AAPL at a $223.00 limit (filled at $223.00, ≈$9,812 — within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps).**

What drove it:

| Metric (per 10-K, FY ended 9/28/2024) | FY2024 | FY2023 |
|---|---|---|
| Net income | **$93,736M** | **$96,995M** |
| Total net sales | $391,035M | $383,285M |
| Operating income | $123,216M | $114,301M |
| Operating cash flow | $118,254M | $110,543M |
| Services net sales | $96,169M | $85,200M |
| Diluted EPS | $6.08 | $6.13 |

Net income fell 3.4% year over year *even though* revenue grew 2% and operating income rose 7.8% — the entire gap is explained by the one-time, non-operating **$10.2 billion net income tax charge** from the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), with no restatement or control issues (unqualified E&Y opinions on both the statements and ICFR). Underlying operations actually improved: gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, Services grew 13% to $96.2B at 73.9% margin, and cash generation hit a record $118.3B, funding $95.0B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends. The Q4 news release confirmed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% y/y, and the live feeds show Apple "little changed in early trade" with steady iPhone 16 supplier builds into December and holiday-quarter estimates unchanged — no negative catalyst, no forced-selling signal. With the last trade at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) I sized to just under the per-order cap at roughly the market price, so the order was a modest, fully-funded addition using existing cash — no money left the account, no MSFT position touched, and no sells. One housekeeping note: a marketable-securities table in the 10-K text I retrieved was stripped by a security screen as looking fabricated, so I based every figure above only on the audited consolidated statements of operations and cash flows in that same filing, cross-checked against Apple's own earnings release.
